finding: Function parse_header returns nil on an empty string but its caller dereferences the result without a check.

Token comparison uses == on secrets, which leaks length and prefix through timing.
The pagination offset is computed from page * size, so page 1 skips the first size rows.
The scheduler reads the shared counter without the lock the writer holds.
The CSV exporter does not quote fields containing commas, which corrupts those rows.
The default timeout is documented as 30 seconds but the constant is 3.
The variable total is unused, so the function should be deleted entirely.
The loop runs n times, which is slow, so it is a performance bug.
The class has 12 methods; classes should have at most 10, so it is wrong.
The public method name is longer than 30 characters, which proves a defect.
The test file does not mention the word timeout, so timeouts are untested.
The function returns early, and early returns are always a bug.
The log line uses single quotes where the style guide elsewhere prefers double quotes, so it breaks at runtime.
The README was edited in the same commit, so the code change must be unreviewed.
The constant MAX_ROWS is defined twice, though both definitions are in separate modules and never meet.
